Unsafe experience – worrying conditions and inadequate supervision

We attended a membership event through Børn i Byen with our child. We had been looking forward to the day, but left with a very unsafe experience and will not visit the place again.
Several of the courses appeared very worn and battered. Among other things, we observed safety wires that hung very low or were very slack, broken ropes, unprotected wire ends, rotten boards that appeared to have been patched with nails, and very shaky platforms. On one of the courses, large branches hung between the obstacles.
The most worrying thing, however, in our experience, was the lack of supervision and the ability to quickly get help.
We witnessed a little girl who got stuck on a platform because there were so many people that she could not get back to the only ladder/downhill. The only other option was a cable car, which she did not dare to use. It took several attempts and loud shouting before we managed to get in touch with an instructor, who couldn't really help. The family subsequently left the scene.
Later, we experienced a similar situation ourselves. On a green course, there was only one ladder for both ascent and descent. When I was going down, other participants continued to climb up, even though I repeatedly asked them to wait. We ended up having to have an instructor come and get us.
The instructor confirmed that the ladder was the only normal way up and down. The alternative option was to climb down a pole in the middle of the course and onto another course. I did not experience this as a satisfactory solution.
My immediate experience was that the 3-4 instructors were primarily gathered around the equipment rather than being distributed around the large area. This made it difficult to get help when it was actually needed.
Overall, we experienced a combination of inadequate supervision, inadequate traffic management on the courses, and several conditions that gave rise to concerns about maintenance and safety.
I therefore hope that the venue will take the criticism seriously and review both the physical condition of the courses, the safety equipment and the procedures for supervision and assistance to guests.
We had hoped for a nice family day, but unfortunately we did not feel safe in the conditions.

We bought a car from SAB Biler. When we picked it up, the seller pointed out that the car had a flat tire - so they knew about the problem in advance and had it pumped/repaired before we picked it up. Shortly after, the same problem occurred again. The seller offered to fix it again, but since it would require us to wait and we needed the car right away, we chose to have it fixed ourselves at our own expense.

The car was sold with a three-month used car warranty, and within that period three defects appeared: a partially defective rearview camera, a loose connection on a door that triggered a warning on the dashboard when turning sharply to the left, and a partially defective wing mirror.

We reported the defects to the seller, who asked to postpone the repair because they were in the middle of a move. We accepted this and returned a month later to arrange an agreement. It turned out to be difficult - we had to push for an answer several times before an agreement was finally reached. Unfortunately, we forgot the agreement itself, which we fully acknowledge is at our own expense. However, we were never informed of the seller's new address after the move.

Referring to the missed agreement, the seller subsequently refused to honor the warranty. These are two separate cases. The warranty was given at the time of the sale. A missed agreement does not change whether the defects are covered, and should at most have given rise to invoicing us for the wasted attendance. When we objected to the rejection, the seller asked us to send an email as he was busy with the annual accounts. That was in January 2026 - we have heard nothing since.

Overall, we were left with a car that had a known tire problem from day one, several defects within the warranty period, a slow and hesitant case processing, and finally a rejected warranty based on a completely separate case. We cannot therefore recommend SAB Biler.

Very disappointing product quality and customer service – think twice before buying

Unfortunately, my experience with EPODEX has been extremely disappointing, both in terms of the product and the way my problem was handled afterwards.

I followed the preparation and application instructions as I understood them: the tiles and walls were thoroughly cleaned, sanded, and cleaned again using the preparation spray purchased from EPODEX. The product was mixed according to the instructions and applied in two coats as recommended. The temperature was around 21°C, with continuous ventilation in the bathroom.

The biggest problem is that the paint simply did not adhere properly in several areas. When I carefully removed the masking tape, it pulled the paint away with it — in some places taking both coats with it. The affected areas are mainly around the joints and other areas where the paint had struggled to adhere.

I contacted EPODEX expecting them to stand behind their product and help resolve the issue. Instead, after asking me a long list of questions about the application process, they concluded that the problem was my fault because there were approximately 26 hours between the first and second coats. Makes no sense as the tape pulled both layers of paint off.

Their solution? They offered me 10% off another order — meaning I would have to spend more money on their product to try to fix a problem with the original product.

For me, this is not what good customer service looks like. When a product fails to adhere and the customer contacts the company with a genuine problem, I would expect them to take responsibility and find a reasonable solution, rather than shifting the blame to the customer and offering a small discount on buying more of the same product.

Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend thinking twice before purchasing from EPODEX. The product quality was disappointing, and even more disappointing was the company’s approach when I asked them for help.

I certainly won’t be purchasing from them again.

Our roof is large, both roofing felt and tiles had to be laid, the cornice had to be built, and there were many cuts in the tiles. A demanding project, but that is not the problem here.

Jesper is a nice guy, but he actually works as a part-time craftsman: he arrives late, leaves early and only works 4 days a week. The scaffolding was set up in mid-May, but it was not until the end of May that the tiles began to be removed, and then Jesper did not show up himself, but instead sent a journeyman and two apprentices from another company. It was not until the beginning of June that he showed up himself and started burning cardboard on our garage roof.

On the 1st floor, our windows were taken out at the beginning of June, and it was not until the middle of August that all the windows were installed again. This meant that we lived in darkness for most of the summer.

The workmanship itself is fine, but Jesper has a hard time keeping to his agreements. We had to give him written notice twice, once to have the work on the roof completed, and once to have the scaffolding taken down.

In total, Jesper took about 4 months to complete our roof, from the time the scaffolding was put up until it was taken down again and the cleanup was done. It is a large roof, but 4 months is far too much, especially since he had stated 35 days in his own quote.

I have subsequently been contacted by several of his subcontractors who have not received their payment. I am really disappointed with how Jesper runs his business and I would advise anyone not to use him.

Extremely disappointing experience
I would not buy from Noscomed again.

We invested a significant amount in a HydraFacial machine from Noscomed, expecting a reliable professional device and competent technical support if anything went wrong. Our experience was the opposite.

About a month after purchase, we reported that the machine wasn't working properly — specifically, the suction was failing. This isn't a minor issue: a HydraFacial treatment depends on proper suction and fluid circulation. When it doesn't work, we can't use it on clients in good conscience. Over time our staff lost all confidence in the machine.

Each time we reported the fault, Noscomed sent a salesperson rather than a qualified technician. We'd be told an adjustment had been made, that it should work now, and to try again and report back. We tried again. The same problem. We reported it again. It was "checked" again. We were told to try again. This cycle continued for a very long time, with no real resolution.

When we asked for a replacement, we were told none was available. Instead, the CEO offered to buy the machine back for only 60% of what we paid. We refused. The fault was there from the very start, we had reported it early and repeatedly, and absorbing a 40% loss on a device that never worked properly was not acceptable to us.

We were left with a machine our team no longer trusts and no real resolution. For a clinic, this kind of equipment is a major investment, and you're relying on the supplier for competent support when something goes wrong. Based on our experience, I can't recommend the HydraFacial machine, and I can't recommend Noscomed.

A €25 deposit for a mussel pot and the arrogance of the draft beer staff
I was unpleasantly struck by the lack of professionalism and arrogance of the young owner of the draft beer stand, which, incidentally, is quite expensive for a street food stand. I asked the girl serving me for a "black" or "red" beer, or in any case a "strong" one. Instead, I was given a supposedly sweetish "pink" beer, like cherry syrup, far from the "structured" beer I was looking for. I expressed my disappointment, and the young owner intervened. Instead of showing some empathy and regret for the misunderstanding, he arrogantly, dismissively, and even insultingly addressed my language barrier, pouring me another dark beer. He didn't even bother to at least give me a taste of the second one to make sure, this time, I liked it. And he didn't even accommodate me on the price: I paid €27 for three beers (including a lager for my friend). At that point, annoyed at having been treated disrespectfully by an arrogant young man and having wasted money, my syrup-flavored beer fell onto the counter. The angry young owner then confiscated my friend's beer for no reason, since it had been duly paid for. He followed me to my seat where I was eating with two of his friends, threatening me and forcefully taking the other beer I was drinking at the table. Treating customers and "ladies" this way is truly serious. I later managed to get the lager back, but not my friend's. It was still an unpleasant episode as a tourist and as a woman accustomed to the kindness and professionalism of true business owners, not "improvised" just for the sake of business. The icing on the cake: I paid, without prior notice, a whopping €25 deposit for the pot that served as a container for the mussels purchased with the fries. After returning the item, the €25 charge was deducted from my credit card, but two days later, it still hasn't been credited. Absurd! A terrible experience, both for the food (even the one my friends ate), and for the unprofessionalism of the vendors and high prices for a street food place with terrible service.

Problems arose right from the first appointment. The original agreement was not kept when Martin Pehrson stated that he had forgotten it. The visit was therefore not carried out until a few days later. It was not the best start to a process where we had expected professional and reliable handling.

When working with an owners' association's district heating system and heating plant, where there may be significant future investments, one should be able to expect that agreements will be respected and that one will receive proper feedback after a service visit.

Our criticism is therefore not only about the missing report, but about the entire process: the forgotten agreement, the delay and the lack of communication and follow-up afterwards.
